notes:
Pass on the fake backend only; the Isaac Lab environment was not run because Isaac Sim 5.1.0 and Isaac Lab 2.3.0 are external Linux/GPU dependencies (README.md:19-23). The package serves the registered unimanual reach environment Isaac-Reach-OpenArm-v0; its native class is the card's OpenArmReachEnvCfg entry symbol because the gym entry_point isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv lies outside the clone. The other card entry symbols (bimanual reach, lift, cabinet) were confirmed to exist but are separate environments and are NOT COVERED. The fake is a pure-Python interface stand-in, never compared with Isaac Lab: its 7-value unbounded joint-position action and 28-value observation are placeholders for the spaces Isaac Lab builds outside the clone, so the package publishes no action envelope and G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is expected; the real action/observation bounds, physics, contacts, sensors, reward terms, rendering, the 4096-environment vectorisation and snapshot/restore are NOT COVERED. The fake's reset offsets, 360-step truncation and 0.0 reward are test data marked placeholder. Expected warnings left in place: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only seeds the next reset), G7.MAYBE_ABSENT x5 (action_space, observation_space, reset, step and close come from the Gymnasium environment base outside the clone), and G8.NO_UNIT x4 (the bridge-derived ticks, action.values and both seed inputs carry no unit). No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. The driver is a simulated R0 device with no hardware backend and never actuates the arm. No hardware run and no human review were performed; driver.lock.json authored_by is the model and reviewed_by is null. DEVIATION FROM CARD: none in shape (family-config GymnasiumDriver); the card's preferred upstream-sim mock path was not runnable here, so a package fake implements the interface instead.
